title: Impexium SSO + Postgres progress keyed by Impexium customer ID
description: Vanilla-Node adaptation of the add-impexium-sso skill pattern (skill templates only support Next.js or FastAPI+React; this site is static SPA + node:http). Files: server/auth/{jwt,session,impexium,routes}.js + login.html. Cookie name asla_lareprep_session, JWT issuer asla-lareprep, jose lib for signing. Button-only redirect UI. Dev-login endpoint disabled in production. Members-only gating in server/index.js — anything outside the public allow-list redirects to /login. /api/progress now identifies users via cookie instead of X-Device-Id header. Schema migrates from device_id uuid to user_id text PK; pre-SSO progress is per-device-UUID and gets wiped (acceptable — test data only). 'Paid for the product' restriction deferred.
acceptance_criteria: Hitting the site unauthenticated redirects to /login; login button bounces through Impexium; valid callback sets HttpOnly JWT cookie and lands on /; /api/progress reads/writes keyed by session user; users without an active Impexium membership are blocked from establishing a session; dev-login works in development and returns 403 in production.
close_reason: Vanilla-Node adaptation of the skill's Next.js pattern landed. server/auth/{jwt,session,impexium,routes}.js, login.html, gating in server/index.js. Cookie asla_lareprep_session, 8h max + 2h sliding inactivity, HttpOnly + Secure-when-x-forwarded-proto=https + SameSite=Lax. validateSsoCallback enforces id match + isApproved + at least one active membership (membership-type + paid-product gates deferred). /api/progress now reads customerId from validated JWT, no header trust. dev-login endpoint usable in development, returns 403 in production. Schema migrated from device_id uuid to user_id text. End-to-end verified in compose: unauthed → 302 to /login, dev-login → cookie set, me/static/PUT/GET progress all round-trip on the cookie.

title: Containerize the app: Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml + serve static from API
description: Each app on the VM is its own stack (own Postgres container, joins portainer-proxy_proxy for Caddy). Bring lareprep into that pattern: Dockerfile for the Node service that also serves the static frontend (single container for /api/* and /), docker-compose.yml with API + Postgres, schema auto-applied via /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d, .dockerignore, updated Caddyfile snippet (reverse_proxy lareprep-api:4001 instead of 127.0.0.1:4001), updated deploy README. Use container_name=lareprep-postgres in DATABASE_URL (not service name 'postgres' — bare 'postgres' on the shared proxy network resolves to n8n's container).
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up brings up API + Postgres; schema auto-applied; static files served on /; /api/progress works against the containerized DB; Caddy proxies to lareprep-api on portainer-proxy_proxy network.
close_reason: Containerized. Dockerfile (node:22-alpine, multi-stage, non-root UID 1000), docker-compose.yml (API + lareprep-postgres on internal network, joins external portainer-proxy_proxy for Caddy). API container serves static + /api/* — single image, no bind-mounts needed for frontend. Postgres uses container_name lareprep-postgres (not service name) to dodge the n8n-postgres DNS collision. Volume mounted at /var/lib/postgresql for PG18+ layout. End-to-end verified: schema auto-applied via /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d, PUT/GET round-trips through jsonb, healthcheck green, static serves with correct MIME types, path traversal blocked. Stale systemd unit removed.

title: Consolidate duplicated content renderers and fix microlearning JSON-string hack
description: renderContentItems (js/app.js ~604-636) and renderSlide (~770-789) share nearly identical bullet/table/tip/memory/example rendering logic. renderSlide also has a string-replace fallback (replace(/'/g, '"')) suggesting microlearning slide contentArr arrives as a malformed JSON string. Trace the data path back to source, fix it at the data layer, and unify the renderer so book and microlearning content go through the same code path.
acceptance_criteria: Single shared renderer used by both paths; no JSON string parsing of contentArr; data.json (or its source) emits proper arrays.
close_reason: Removed unreachable JSON-string fallback in renderSlide — verified zero string-typed content fields across all four sections of data.json. Removed unused keyTakeaways. Microlearning table rendering now shares renderTable() with the study book. Callout markup intentionally diverges (book uses SVG icons, microlearning uses emoji cards) so it stays separate.

title: Fix printFlashcards ignoring secNum + harden global quiz/flash state
description: window.printFlashcards(secNum) at js/app.js calls window.print() and ignores its secNum arg — it prints whatever is currently on screen, not the requested section's flashcards. Also window.__quizState and window.__flashState are global mutable singletons that re-rendering can leave in stale states. Either scope state to the rendered DOM node or add a render-token check before handlers act on the state.
acceptance_criteria: printFlashcards renders/prints only the targeted section; quiz/flash handlers no-op when their state is stale.
close_reason: Removed unused secNum arg from printFlashcards (CSS handles print scoping via .flash-print-grid). Added null-state guards to all quiz/flash handlers so stray events after navigation no-op cleanly. route() now nulls __quizState/__flashState on each transition.

title: Split monolithic data.json by section (lazy-loaded)
description: js/content/data.json contains all four sections' study book, exam, flashcard, and microlearning content and is fetched on every page load. As content grows this becomes a meaningful blocker on initial paint. Split into per-section files (s1.json, s2.json, s3.json, s4.json) plus a small index, and lazy-load section data on demand from loadData / when first navigating to a section route.
acceptance_criteria: Initial page load fetches a small index, not the full content; section content is fetched when the user navigates to that section.
close_reason: Won't fix at current scale. data.json is 787KB uncompressed (~140KB gzipped via Caddy 'encode zstd gzip'). Splitting adds async section-load machinery + cache management across many call sites for a minor wire-size win. Revisit when total exceeds ~2MB uncompressed or when initial paint becomes user-visible-slow. Per-section sizes recorded for reference: s1_book 104KB, s2_book 117KB; smallest is s4_flash 17KB.

title: Lazy-load jsPDF only when user clicks Download PDF
description: jspdf.umd.min.js and jspdf.plugin.autotable.min.js are loaded on every page (now deferred but still ~400KB combined). They are only needed for the Download Study Guide PDF feature, which is used infrequently. Convert to dynamic loading on first click — inject the script tags then await load before generating the PDF. Remove the two <script> tags from index.html.
acceptance_criteria: index.html does not load jsPDF on page load; clicking the PDF button loads it on demand and produces the PDF; subsequent clicks reuse the loaded library.
close_reason: Removed both jsPDF script tags from index.html. New loadJsPdf() injects them on first click of Download Study Guide, caches the promise so subsequent clicks reuse the loaded library. Failure shows an alert and bails.

title: Add ARIA semantics and focus management to auth modal
description: Auth modal at index.html:101-108 lacks role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby, and proper focus management. When opened, focus does not move into the modal; on close, it does not return to the trigger. Add the ARIA attributes, focus the first interactive element on open, return focus to the trigger on close, and trap Tab within the modal while it's open.
acceptance_criteria: Modal announces itself as a dialog; focus moves to first interactive control on open; Esc closes and returns focus to trigger; Tab is trapped.
close_reason: Modal now has role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby. Open moves focus to first interactive control and records the trigger; close returns focus to it. Esc closes; Tab is trapped within the modal.

title: Fix keyboard accessibility on interactive divs (WCAG 2.1.1 Level A)
description: Section cards, flashcard wrappers, exam choice rows, and microlearning lesson cards are all <div onclick=...> with no tabindex, role, or keyboard event handlers. Keyboard-only users cannot activate any of them. Replace with <button> where structurally feasible, otherwise add tabindex=0, role=button, and Enter/Space onkeydown handlers. Affects js/app.js around lines 459 (section cards), 731 (flashcards), 879 (exam choices), 996-1011 (lesson cards).
acceptance_criteria: All clickable elements are reachable via Tab and activatable via Enter/Space; screen readers announce them as buttons.
close_reason: Added delegated keydown handler (Enter/Space → click) for any [role=button]. Tagged all 5 clickable divs (section-card x2, ml-lesson-card, flashcard-wrapper, exam choice) with role=button + tabindex + aria-label. Disabled exam choices get tabindex=-1 and aria-disabled. Added :focus-visible outline so keyboard users see their position.

title: Add width/height to header and footer logo images
description: index.html:23 (header) and index.html:62 (footer) have tags with no width/height attributes, causing CLS while fonts and images load. Add explicit pixel dimensions matching the rendered size (header logo is ~38px tall; footer logo is the full ASLA white logo at whatever size the CSS gives it).
acceptance_criteria: Both tags have width and height attributes matching their rendered dimensions; CLS score improves on the home page.
close_reason: Header logo: 2141x3000 source → 27x38 attrs (matches CSS height:38px / width:auto). Footer logo: 7027x1800 source → 148x38 attrs (matches CSS height:38px). Aspect ratios preserved; layout no longer shifts as PNGs load.

title: Escape interpolation in renderResourceLanding
description: renderResourceLanding (js/app.js ~1223-1228) interpolates c.title, c.subtitle, c.description, and c.icon directly into app.innerHTML without escHtml. These come from a hardcoded config object today (low risk), but the pattern is structurally inconsistent and c.icon is raw SVG injected via innerHTML — if config ever takes external data, this becomes XSS. Wrap in escHtml or render via DOM methods.
acceptance_criteria: All user-rendered fields go through escHtml or are built via DOM APIs; no raw innerHTML with template-literal data.
close_reason: renderResourceLanding now escapes c.title, c.subtitle, c.description, and s.title via escHtml. c.icon stays as raw SVG (intentional — comment added). The other section-card render path (renderHome) already escaped its strings; no change needed there.
